1	import XCTest
2	
3	@testable import Workroom
4	
5	/// `CLIVCSWriter` against REAL git and jj repos through the REAL `StatusCommandRunner`.
6	///
7	/// **No network.** Every "remote" is a bare repo on disk reached over `file://`, so fetch, push and
8	/// pull are genuine end-to-end operations with no credentials, no rate limits and no flakiness. Every
9	/// repo is a throwaway under `NSTemporaryDirectory()`, removed in `tearDown` — these never touch a
10	/// developer's own repositories.
11	///
12	/// Two tests here exist specifically to pin bugs that shipped in the design and were caught in review:
13	/// - `testCountsAreIdenticalUnderEveryPushDefault` — the original design read ahead/behind from
14	///   `%(push:track)`, which is EMPTY for a branch with no upstream under git's default
15	///   `push.default=simple`, i.e. for every `git worktree add -b` workroom.
16	/// - `testFetchAtTheRootMovesAWorkroomsLastFetchLabel` — `FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so fetching at
17	///   the project root never writes the workroom's copy; reading the wrong one meant "never fetched"
18	///   forever.
19	final class VCSRemoteIntegrationTests: XCTestCase {
20	  private var dirs: [String] = []
21	  private var exportedJJConfig = false
22	
23	  override func tearDown() {
24	    for d in dirs { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(atPath: d) }
25	    dirs = []
26	    if exportedJJConfig {
27	      unsetenv("JJ_CONFIG")
28	      exportedJJConfig = false
29	    }
30	    super.tearDown()
31	  }
32	
33	  // MARK: helpers
34	
35	  /// Point **this process** at a fixture's jj config, so the jj the app spawns reads it too.
36	  ///
37	  /// `sh` prefixes `JJ_CONFIG=` onto its own command line, which covers fixture setup and nothing else:
38	  /// `StatusCommandRunner` seeds a child's environment from `ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment`, and
39	  /// jj-lib's config chain (`jj_config.rs`) reads `$JJ_CONFIG` at call time — so without this every
40	  /// app-driven jj read and write in this file runs against the DEVELOPER's `~/.config/jj/config.toml`.
41	  ///
42	  /// That is what made `testAnonymousJJPushCreatesATrackedPushBookmark` pass locally and fail on CI. A
43	  /// runner has no jj identity, so the snapshot jj takes as part of `jj git push` rewrote `@` with an
44	  /// EMPTY committer and jj then refused its own bookmark: "Won't push commit … since it has no author
45	  /// and/or committer set". Pinning the config fixes the identity, and also makes a developer's own
46	  /// `templates.git_push_bookmark` (or any other jj customisation) unable to reach these assertions.
47	  ///
48	  /// Process-wide mutation is safe here: XCTest runs a test process's tests serially — parallel testing
49	  /// distributes test *classes* across processes — and `tearDown` clears it either way.
50	  private func exportJJConfig(_ path: String) {
51	    setenv("JJ_CONFIG", path, 1)
52	    exportedJJConfig = true
53	  }
54	
55	  private func tool(_ name: String) -> Bool {
56	    sh("command -v \(name)", in: NSTemporaryDirectory()).exit == 0
57	  }
58	
59	  private struct MissingTool: Error { let name: String }
60	  private func requireTool(_ name: String) throws {
61	    if !tool(name) {
62	      XCTFail("`\(name)` is required for integration tests; CI installs it (brew install \(name))")
63	      throw MissingTool(name: name)
64	    }
65	  }
66	
67	  private func tempDir() -> String {
68	    let d = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "wr-remote-\(UUID().uuidString)"
69	    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: d, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
70	    dirs.append(d)
71	    return d
72	  }
73	
74	  @discardableResult
75	  private func sh(_ cmd: String, in dir: String) -> (out: String, exit: Int32) {
76	    let p = Process()
77	    p.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/bin/sh")
78	    p.arguments = ["-c", cmd]
79	    p.currentDirectoryURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: dir)
